sites.name: Mahale Mountains National Park
sites.summary: Forested mountains dropping into crystal-clear Lake Tanganyika – chimps, lake shore birding and West African range extensions in remote western Tanzania.
whyItMatters: One of Africa’s great lakeshore wilderness parks – forest and freshwater habitats in one compact block.
Western forest bird communities overlap with the Congo basin on selected species.
Ideal western finale after Katavi or Gombe on specialist forest-and-lake itineraries.
sites.generalNotes: Boat transfers on Tanganyika and guided forest walks define the birding pace here.

sites.name: Gombe Stream National Park
sites.summary: Tiny, steep rainforest park famous for chimpanzees – tight forest trails with rich understory birdlife on the lake escarpment.
whyItMatters: Classic Jane Goodall chimp country with equally rewarding forest birding on narrow ridge trails.
Boat access on Tanganyika links lake-level waterbirds with montane forest species in one day.
Pairs naturally with Mahale on western forest birding safaris.
sites.generalNotes: Steep hiking – birding is on foot with guide-led listening stops.

sites.name: Katavi National Park
sites.summary: Raw, remote floodplains and miombo – enormous hippo and buffalo concentrations with open-country and woodland birding far from crowds.
whyItMatters: Among Tanzania’s least visited big parks – authentic wilderness birding and wildlife.
Seasonal Lake Katavi and Katisunga Plains concentrate birds and mammals dramatically.
Core western anchor on 10-day south-west routes linking to Mahale or Ruaha extensions.
sites.generalNotes: Dry-season concentrations are legendary; green season brings different breeders and migrants.

sites.name: Rubondo Island National Park
sites.summary: Forest island on Lake Victoria – reintroduced chimps, shy sitatunga and a mix of lake, papyrus and gallery forest birds.
whyItMatters: Unique island ecosystem on Africa’s largest lake – different feel from mainland parks.
Forest walks and boat trips combine for varied daily birding.
Often paired with western lake routes or fly-in extensions from Mwanza.
sites.generalNotes: Boat logistics from Kasenda or Mwanza define access; pace is relaxed and exploratory.

sites.name: Burigi-Chato National Park
sites.location: Kagera Region · Lake Burigi & savanna woodlands
sites.summary: Newer western park mosaic of lakes, savanna and woodland – growing reputation for quiet game viewing and regional bird diversity.
whyItMatters: Expands Tanzania’s western birding map beyond Mahale–Gombe with open-country and lake habitats.
Featured on Endemic Birds’ 9-day western forest-and-lake birding itinerary.
Low visitor numbers mean undisturbed scanning along lake shores and game tracks.
sites.generalNotes: Often combined with Minziro forest and Mahale on north-western birding loops.

sites.name: Minziro Forest Reserve
sites.location: Kagera Region · Uganda border lowland forest
sites.summary: Tanzania’s largest lowland forest – Congo–Guinea biome species at the edge of their range, central to western endemic birding routes.
whyItMatters: Critical Important Bird Area linking eastern Africa to Congolian forest avifauna.
Anchor site on the published 9-day Mahale–Gombe–Burigi–Minziro birding itinerary.
Essential for listers seeking western forest species rarely seen on northern or southern circuits.
sites.generalNotes: Forest interior birding with local guides; often accessed from the Kagera / Minziro village area.
